items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: the blues was good enough for Louis Armstrong man, and good enough for Charlie Parker, and good enough for Roy Eldridge and Coleman Hawkins

ctx.x: No. And so I mean the blues was good enough for Louis Armstrong man, and good enough for Charlie Parker, and good enough for Roy Eldridge and Coleman Hawkins, and Prez, and all of these cats, all the way through Miles, Clifford Brown, Diz, and then kind of all of a sudden it started to diminish when we could justify that we really wanted to get serious or whatever. And I think blues is serious man, it’s very serious. Because it’s something from within, not something acquired. It’s a statement from within.
Well I’m sure you’re going to keep it alive in your own playing.
